title: Network diffusion model predicts neurodegeneration in limb-onset Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis.
authors: Bhattarai, Anjan; Chen, Zhaolin; Chua, Phyllis; Talman, Paul; Mathers, Susan; Chapman, Caron; Howe, James; Lee, C M Sarah; Lie, Yenni; Poudel, Govinda R; Egan, Gary F
one_liner_zh: 该文用网络扩散模型预测肌萎缩侧索硬化症中的神经退行性变，研究对象为脑连接组与MRI萎缩模式，完全不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合，与本课题无关。
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Emerging evidences suggest that the trans-neural propagation of phosphorylated 43-kDa transactive response DNA-binding protein (pTDP-43) contributes to neurodegeneration in Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS). We investigated whether Network Diffusion Model (NDM), a biophysical model of spread of pathology via the brain connectome, could capture the severity and progression of neurodegeneration (atrophy) in ALS. METHODS: We measured degeneration in limb-onset ALS patients (n = 14 at baseline, 12 at 6-months, and 9 at 12 months) and controls (n = 12 at baseline) using FreeSurfer analysis on the structural T1-weighted Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) data. The NDM was simulated on the canonical structural connectome from the IIT Human Brain Atlas. To determine whether NDM could predict the atrophy pattern in ALS, the accumulation of pathology modelled by NDM was correlated against atrophy measured using MRI. In order to investigate whether network spread on the brain connectome derived from healthy individuals were significant findings, we compared our findings against network spread simulated on random networks. RESULTS: The cross-sectional analyses revealed that the network diffusion seeded from the inferior frontal gyrus (pars triangularis and pars orbitalis) significantly predicts the atrophy pattern in ALS compared to controls. Whereas, atrophy over time with-in the ALS group was best predicted by seeding the network diffusion process from the inferior temporal gyrus at 6-month and caudal middle frontal gyrus at 12-month. Network spread simulated on the random networks showed that the findings using healthy brain connectomes are significantly different from null models. INTERPRETATION: Our findings suggest the involvement of extra-motor regions in seeding the spread of pathology in ALS. Importantly, NDM was able to recapitulate the dynamics of pathological progression in ALS. Understanding the spatial shifts in the seeds of degeneration over time can potentially inform further research in the design of disease modifying therapeutic interventions in ALS.
abstract_zh: 目的：新近证据表明，磷酸化43 kDa反式激活反应性DNA结合蛋白（pTDP-43）的跨神经传播有助于肌萎缩侧索硬化症（ALS）中的神经退行性变。我们研究了网络扩散模型（NDM），一种通过脑连接组传播病理的生物物理模型，是否能捕捉ALS中神经退行性变（萎缩）的严重性和进展。方法：我们使用FreeSurfer分析结构性T1加权磁共振成像（MRI）数据，测量了肢体起病ALS患者（基线时n=14，6个月时n=12，12个月时n=9）和对照组（基线时n=12）的退行性变。NDM在来自IIT人脑图谱的典型结构连接组上进行了模拟。为确定NDM是否能预测ALS中的萎缩模式，我们将NDM模拟的病理积累与MRI测量的萎缩进行了相关性分析。为探究源自健康个体的脑连接组上的网络传播是否具有显著意义，我们将我们的发现与在随机网络上模拟的网络传播进行了比较。结果：横断面分析显示，从额下回（三角部和眶部）起始的网络扩散显著预测了ALS中与对照组相比的萎缩模式。而ALS组内随时间变化的萎缩，在6个月时由颞下回起始的网络扩散过程预测最佳，在12个月时由尾侧中额回起始的预测最佳。在随机网络上模拟的网络传播显示，使用健康脑连接组的结果与零模型显著不同。解释：我们的发现提示，ALS中病理传播的起始涉及运动外区域。重要的是，NDM能够重现ALS病理进展的动态过程。理解退行性变起始点随时间的空间转移，可能为ALS疾病修饰治疗干预的设计提供进一步研究参考。
